First off I'd like to state that I was given a press copy and have played this game *extensively* - About 20ish hours in the first playthrough of NG. I've also got a LOT of experience with 'Soulslike' games and have even done things like SL1 runs in DS and NG+7 on Bloodborne.
I'm straight out listing this game as a 4/10 before I start. I do not suggest buying it in the current state it is in.
I've already done a full 'spoken' review of the game after streaming it from start to finish. You can find that here if you'd prefer a verbal review. -
I'm going to do this with bullet points listing pros and cons. We're going to start with the positives of the game.
PROS
-------------
-The game is visually appealing and retains high graphical quality. The character especially looks fantastic when you're plowing through in power armor. A lot of the weapons are also extremely attractive to look at.
-It has a great concept. The idea of 'futurey sci-fi Darksouls' is an appealing one. The idea of it involving exosuits is even cooler.
-It appeals to anyone who particularly enjoys grinding for long periods of time without progression. It's an extremely grindy game.
-It has SOME BASIC concepts of combat that are enjoyable for a little while. The game feels good for about three hours.
-SOME of the story/lore objects are interesting to listen to and establish a 'basic' understanding of the universe. I liked what little I got.
That's where the positives end. The negatives are staggering so bare with me.
CONS
-------------
-The combat is extremely clunky. Combos have 'queue' systems which results in you doing things you didn't intend to do. You cannot cancel combo chains. Anything heavy takes quite some time to use/swing and it results in you doing quite a few 'single strike' attacks. Multiple enemies are not limited to the same clunky mechanics. A lot of them have almost instantaneous-instadeath attacks.
-Enemies have hyper armor. Most enemies can straight up ignore any assault you're delivering to them due to a game mechanic called "impact". This mechanic makes most light and quick weapons useless as you CANNOT trade with enemies effectively.  Even the most powerful weapons in the game do not stagger throughout combos and results in you being struck repeatedly. Enemies, even weaker ones, will power through your attacks and royally kick your butt. This applies to EVERY enemy.
-Deaths feel cheated due to 'cheesy' mechanics. A lot of the time you die you'll feel as if it was cheaty. A lot of enemy 'downtimes' are bugged right now which results in them IMMEDIATELY recovering from a stagger or attack. This 'hyperarmor' results in you dying a lot more than you should and makes you feel underpowered in almost every situation early on. A lot of the enemy types have lunges which TRACK MID AIR and deal 120+ damage which results in an almost instantaneous death at any point. These enemies are common throughout the entire game.
-The game has no real 'story' or objectives. There's no guidance. There's no cutscenes. There's no waypoint system. You will spend a LOT of time wandering around wondering what is going on. You will never have the answers to who you are or why you're in the facility. You will never see ANY sort of change in the main game based on helping people out or doing bonus side quests. A lot of time will be spent running back and forth trying to find an unlisted objective you need to progress. The ending is not satisfying at all.
-Leveling up virtually does nothing. It's almost impossible to 'power up' in an area you're having issues with. If you're having issues fighting in an area you CANNOT increase your power through means of leveling. Upgrading your power core does not increase your strength, stats, health, or damage. This results in a 'hitting a wall' feeling in some areas and forces you to skip large packs of enemies. Gear progression is gated. This also means you CANNOT specialize in one type of weapon to make it better with stats.
-There is only really one 'viable' way to fight each enemy. Trying to do combos or trading blows will result in your death. The majority of my entire playthrough (Through sheer death) was nothing but dash-attacks then dodging out as getting hit was bad. I couldn't use any of the neat combos that a lot of the weapons had simply because you were punished FAAAAR too hard for doing so.
-The grind is not justified. It is not worth it. There's not much to say here. You get tier 6 things in NG+ if you play it so everything is invalidated. You'll spend hours killing one set of mobs for specific things only to find out that the bonus is garbage and the set is not that good.
-Level design is EXTREMELY repetitive. There are only six real levels throughout the entire game. SIX LEVELS WITH BACKTRACKING. Same hallways. Same corridors. Same walls. Same enemies. Same pretty much everything (until the end, it's kinda cool)
-There is a LOT of backtracking and running. You will be running back from death a LOT. There is no fast travel mechanic. There is no homeward bone. Tech scrap (souls) have a preset timer you have to beat to get back to them or they vanish. You will spend literal hours by the end of the game simply running back after deaths. Shortcuts help but it is still an immense flaw in the game's design. It's not fun. There are also containers at the BEGINNING OF THE GAME which require absurd power core levels to open that you will have to travel back to later. Again, more backtracking.
-The 'bonfire' system is flawed. There is only one per level and there is no way to immediately travel back and store your 'souls'. This is an immense annoyance throughout the game. You never really get a 'checkpoint' through levels that take quite some time to go through. Dark Souls got it right with pacing and a lot of the time you had moments of rest when needed.. this gives no such relief.
-There are only five bosses in the entire game. Five. Bosses. One of them is pretty much a repeat of another one. Their last game LORDS OF THE FALLEN had 11, I believe? This is a complete step backwards. Also, none of them are particularly unique or interesting.
-The boss weapon mechanic is awful and there are no savefiles to remedy a screwup. Bosses drop a specific unique weapon when they die. This weapon can be awful if you don't do a 'specific' challenge during the fight to power it up. There's no way to re-do this to get the better weapon unless you start a new game. There are no save files. You cannot repeat bosses if you make a mistake. Most players will not know that this is even the case.. and you will not want to do NG+ in most cases.
-Weapon proficiency hurts the game. It's similar to an MMO mechanic which serves no purpose. This stat invalidates most of the weapons the player can use from being useful. You have to spend hours killing enemies to 'level up' a proficiency (staves, single rigged, dual rigged, one handed, heavy weapon) to make them viable. If you get a great weapon from a boss but you haven't used that 'type' the entire game: it will be garbage. Later on grinding proficiency is terrible as enemies have a LOT of armor and unleveled proficiencies cannot hurt or damage them enough. It's an MMO mechanic that was not good for this game at all.
.... Honestly I could nitpick and explain a lot more in detail but I don't really see the need.
This was a step backwards in my opinion from Lords of the Fallen. I believe a lot of 'reviews' and 'impressions' have only seen the first few hours of the game. It takes a nosedive after the first few hours straight into the ground.
It tries far too hard to copy Dark Souls in some ways and the game suffers because of it.
Again, 4/10 - do not buy full price. Go play Lords of the Fallen by this company for 10 bucks.

Pros: Free to Play. Brought some successful elements from Ragnarok Online, which I enjoyed. Graphics Updated from RO, but.. Good flexibility for hot keys. Many premium items can be obtained in-game, but..
Cons: The list of cons is huge.
1. Graphics are updated, but .. mediocre by today's photorealistic qualities.
2. It is definitely a free to play, but PAY TO WIN, model. In comparing the relative speed at which pay users achieve end game characters and equipment, I would estimate that the pay players are at least 5 times faster to achieve their goals over the average free player. This is evident by players who have started around the same time as me (free player), but have already been miles ahead of me in a matter of days, and I'm not one of the average free players, myself. Likewise, many who play much less, are already left behind in the dust.
3. Grinding end game levels will definitely put you on your knees, and that's even with a premium membership. Yea, lots of level grinding. I've heard of a L55 premium sniper complain about it. And when you see L22~26 players grinding on L50+ mobs..and the max level is L60..you know, something is wrong here. When you die, above L20, you are exposed to a 10 minute status ailment called weakness, that halves your attack and defence. The only way to get rid of it immediately is to pay the npcs gold, gold that escalates every level higher than L20 you are. So each time you respawn, you've got to do something else to wait out the weakness time..otherwise cough up (or go premium, which reduces that time to 1 min).
4. Earning in-game currency is really horrendous. It's subtle, but with a closer look, you'll see that the loot that you bring in from the monsters, especially true for the higher levels, are not only few, but they hardly add up to buy a single health potion of equivalent level. The rest of the loot can be vended, but only with a time-restricted stall that you need to purchase for more coin..So what does this mean? It simply means, you'll have to farm loot with minimum potions/foods most of the time unless you can successfully fetch a good price for your vended goods. Other times, you'll have to rely solely on the gold earned through quests, and there aren't that many well paying quests after you've completed your main ones. On top of all that, if you've got weakness, you've got to wait it out before you can even start farming for loot.
5. PvP everywhere, if you're a friendly, social player like myself, you'll hate the PvP, but that's fine of course, if it's confined to themselves and we PvEer are left to our own entertainment. Sadly, that is not entirely true. The guild system has a lot of perks, like discounted npc prices, better drop rates, better running speed, more defence, more attack and a social community. However, past rank 10, and the guild is prone to other guilds declaring war on it. Some high level players have decided to band together in a certain guild (unnamed, but it could be anyone) in an effort to extort protection tax from smaller guilds so that they will not be PKed outside of towns..it's kind of like how the triads extorts everyday citizens.
I guess this is a reflection of the situations real Russians face..but still..
THIS IS A BIG DOWNER.
6. A massive rip off from the once popular Ragnarok Online. Not that, that in itself is a bad thing, since they had done a lot of concepts right. And most games these days are copied from one another. Big Deal.

I have played Heroes of WW2, Men of War, Men of War Assault Squad, and Men of War Assault Squad 2. I think I have a good grasp of the games, with MOW: AS being my favorite (Over 400 hours in that game).
Someone said, this game looks good, and naturally because I've played for so long, I gave it a shot. I was sorely disapointed.
Men of War: Assault Squad (MOW:AS) completely changed the game. It was the first of the series that introduced the squad system, first of the games that introduced heroic units, streamlined the game play and made it fast paced. The selection of units were great, with different weapons for different nations, on top of tanks and other distinct advantages. It only got better from there with MOW: AS2. Better graphics, steam matchmaking, rankings, and a good amount of updates.
So with things getting better and better, I expected this to be in line. New concepts, new heroes, new abilities, different tactics. Right? Nope. At the moment, you are presented with a reskined MOW: AS.
So let's talk about the game on it's own merit. Arty has imensely high lethality. Some might say this is a good thing, and I respect that, but for me all it does is increase the reliance on arty instead of managing the men up front. The heavy arty does come later in the game, with tanks making appearences before the heavy guns. With such lethality, you care less about your men. Tanks? Clumsy, and while it may represent the historical setting, the fact of the matter is there. You have a small unit pool. The interace is garbage. Any improvement on the interface? NOPE.
Armour penetration chances? I have yet to see it. Messages about damaged parts on a vehicles? Yet to see it.
The game focuses a lot on infantry, and emplacement/light guns to get people out of areas. A different type of shell (Shrapnel) that explodes over the area is a simple grenade type ability to stop people from camping, or to counter MG's. It's my line vs yours, as I'll position my arty and blast whatever I see. Snorefest.
There really isn't anything else to talk about. The Campaign is pretty bland, it's tough to form an attachment with terrible voice overs that can die in seconds. Some people might like the campaign, I persoanlly didn't like shooting a bunch of men trying to attack a line. For now, DON'T BUY THIS GAME. It brings nothing new to the table, aside from a horse unit, and a shrapnel shot that arty unit's can use.

Transistor has one of the most unique combat systems of any game I've played. It is both a combination of real time action combined with turned based strategy. What makes this interesting is that you can activate turned based combat at any time, but it comes at a big cost. After you execute a "turn", it is put on a cooldown where most (or all) of your abilities become unavailable for a short time. This makes you very vulnerable to the enemy and creates a very interesting risk/reward type combat system. Do you fight in realtime and suffer from slow attack swings? Or do you take a "turn" getting off those attacks for free, but suffer a large and vulnerable downtime?
Additionally, any ability can be "equipped" to any other ability to modify how it works. Your fast bolt attack can be "equipped" to another attack to make it shoot faster for instance. This gives so many unique combinations of attacks that it's quite overwhelming at first. This dynamic setting of attacks is really rewarding as it feels like your attacks are unique to you. And it allows for a vast amount of different playstyles which keeps combat fresh. You can switch from a heavy hitting melee to a long range mage to a stealthy backstabbing rogue.
But that's not all Transistor has to offer. The backgrounds are beautiful, the voice acting is great, the atmosphere is amazing, the artstyle is sublime, and the story really brings it all together. The mystery of it all keeps you craving for more to make it a true beautiful work of art.

This is, without a doubt, the most beautiful game I have ever played. And it could also easily be the most beautiful game I will ever play. It is a peice of art. Everything about this game is magnificant, perhaps even perfect - The artwork is gorgeous, the storyline is elegant and, in the end, bittersweet. The gameplay is smooth and intuitive, and the music is heavenly and, quite honestly, breathtaking (as such, perhaps unsurprisingly, I firmly recommend purchasing the SoundTrack, too).
This is a game that should be experienced by as many people as possible. It's a masterpiece.
(EDIT: This game got my vote for the: The “I'm Not Crying, There's Something In My Eye” Award in the 2016 Steam Awards, which shoudl give you an idea of my emotional investment).
PS: The soundtrack is amazing!

While I've heard great things about this game, and I'm sure the gameplay is pretty good, I was unable to enjoy this game as it is very poorly optimized for how it looks. With an i5 6600K, a GTX 1070, and 16 GB of RAM, I get 35-55 fps in 1440p with all setting maxed out. Turning the settings down gives me an increase of 15-20 fps. GTA V with everything but MSAA and Grass maxed out and no soft shadows gives me 110-130 fps in 1440p. Battlefield 1 with everything maxed out gives me 70-85 fps in 1440p. And those three games look a lot better than this game, though Sleeping Dogs Definitive Edition does look pretty good for a remaster from 2014 for a game from 2012. I noticed that this seems to be a common issue, with people with GTX 1060s struggling to get 40 fps in 1080p. And I heard that the original with a free texture pack released by the developer to make the two games look identical performs much better than this game, so it's obviously just a poorly optimized game. Shallow, repetitive, and really just not much fun.
Play 10 minutes and you've experienced all this game has to offer, and it's unlikely it'll be enough to compel you to return for a rerun.
- The sudden shifts between activities feels gimmicky, abruptly ending the action and feeling frustrating rather than the "sense of random chaos" the game boasts. There's no fun in splitting up an activity into pieces that are played out in  short sprints.
- There's comparisons being made to Mario Party and the like but this game doesn't offer that feeling at all. Imagine playing a Mario Party mini-activity where halfway through an activity it suddenly switched to another activity, made you play 1/3 of that 2nd activity, and then swapped to a new one, only to return to where you left off in the first activity with no sense of progress, accomplishment, or the build up of excitement.
- Now imagine that eliminated players could still repeatedly hit you and remove the points you've earned in a game, in a "juggling-style" manner where you can't escape their onslaught because they're invincible, making it impossible to win as the skilled player, instead leaving it to the player's (grudging) personal preference in who should win.
- Even the activities feel unfinished. This game feels like an early access game, with activities having visual appeal but no polish to the gameplay. Each activity feels rushed to production, guided by attractive art alone, without thought to what makes an activity fun. 12 players at a "party games" event and not a single one of them enjoyed these activities. The agreement was they were shiny turds that were equal parts frustrating and boring.
- The sounds are annoying. Imagine the high-pitched voices of cartoon characters repeated endlessly in every activity, making the same "hit" noises over and over until all you hear is "oof ah eeee oh umf eh eh oof" for the entire duration of play. The music might be tolerable (at best) but combined with the SFX it equals nothing more than noise.
- It just doesn't cut it as an enjoyable party game, would never work as a "take that" competitive game, and just all over reeks of bad design and ineffective (if there was any) user experience playtesting hidden beneath an impressive (and grossly misleading) art budget.
Pass on this one. Full out not recommended.

Now that I completed the game, let me start by saying I still recommend the game, but will bring up a few issues that I experienced (This is NOT a review, just a list of problems others may face if they choose to purchase):
1) Level design is far too narrow for the combat style. In certain areas it was nearly impossible to not get stuck somewhere due to this, especially the latter half of the game this became even more obvious.
2) Enemies are more than just difficult, it is easy to be one, two or three-shotted by any enemy in the game. This causes a problem in that you can't make a mistake in any fight otherwise you will risk dying. Dark Souls enemies are tough but fair, The Surge just wants you to run through certain areas like a gauntlet match due to level design + enemy damage.
3) There are only five bosses, but due to my #2 issue, I am glad there are only 5. Outside of the first two bosses, the last three are amped up in difficulty to ridiculous measures. They are more frustrating than they are fun to fight, and although the last boss was invigorating to defeat, most of the time I just wanted  these fights to be over with and move on.
4) Whilst I thought the storyline was good, I felt there were plot holes that were never filled, including side quests. One of the biggest anticlimactic letdowns you will experience will be near the end of the game.
5) Low amount of different builds available. All melee, no ranged or "magic" is here, which I knew when I got into the game. But the Drone you get early on is very useless throughout the game. I was hoping I could upgrade it, maybe if someone wanted to do a Drone-focused build that could have been the ranged option, but unfortunately even with the different abilities you find for it later, the energy cost is just never worth it when energy can be used for so many other important things.
5.2) Speaking of low amount of builds, the game forces you to stick to a specific weapon type due to the "proficiency" level. Initially I thought it was a good idea to help people who die often but still have some sense of progression, but really you won't use any other kind of weapon since proficiency takes quite a while to level up, and it does have some significant impact to how much damage you can do. I kept going through the game saying, "I'll level up one slow weapon and one fast weapon." but all I did was stick with Heavy-Duty throughout.
5.3) I know I keep going on about this, but it's important for replay value, which this game has little of unfortunately. So to top off the low build volume, you also have very few useful weapons. Boss weapons you get pretty much triumph over any other drop you will find in the game, except maybe for one weapon. So once again you will be limited to a handful of viable weapons, then one specific one due to proficiency.
Those were the biggest issues I discovered, but despite the negatives, it is still a pretty decent game and gave me about 25 hours out of my $45. I will revisit this if they ever add DLC or fix some of the build issues with the game.

Firstly: I have around 15 hours in this game, but I was not using Steam.
I, like many, played EV Nova back when I was young, and it crawled into a corner of my heart and never left. This game, Endless Sky, has done more than scratch an itch I forgot I had - it has reawakened a part of my childhood. It is a beautiful successor to EV Nova - still a work in progress, but already very polished, and FOSS to boot, a perk that cannot be overstated.
Simply put, if you loved EV Nova, you need to play this game. If you didn't, you might not 'get it'. This is a recreation of a game from the early 2000's created mostly by a single developer, so don't expect a highly-polished, content-heavy game with beautiful graphics. At least, not yet. That said, I haven't had a single crash in 15 hours of gameplay. My CPU runs like it's idling. The gui is cohesive, the art style is there, the writing is very good, sounds could use some work but they're no worse than EV Nova, controls are, well, pretty crappy by default but they're configurable. There are very few bugs, and I haven't hit any major ones.
At the time of writing, there is only one major campaign, but it is long. I don't know how long because, after 15 hours (including a lot of messing around), I haven't finished it yet. Best of all, because the game is open-source, anybody is free to contribute content or provide fixes.
In summary: Thank you, developer. This game is a gift.

Simply the best puzzle game series you're going to find. Hexcells Infinite is the best of the three, but working your way from the first game to the third (with its prize of an unending number of puzzles) brings as much satisfaction as the puzzles themselves.
Instead of being repetitive and mind-numbing, the Hexcells games are ones you can relax into and play for hours without tiring of them. Unlike most logic puzzles they maintain difficulty levels and continually present challenges without ever relying on guesswork.
This entire series is a must-have for anyone who enjoys logic puzzles.

Hexcells Infinite is a fitting conclusion to the Hexcells trifecta. The campaign boasts some of the most difficult hand-crafted puzzles seen in the series, and
, thanks to an abbreviated tutorial. (You really are expected to have already familiarized yourself with the mechanics via the previous two Hexcells installments.) The new Infinite Mode is a fantastic new feature, producing a near-endless barrage of randomly generated puzzles. It's immediatley obvious that the random puzzles are not as difficult as the hand-crafted campaign puzzles (the constructions leave far too many unnecessary hints), but it's nice to have something different to sic the ol' brain on each evening.
If you've enjoyed the first two Hexcells installments, you simply must get Hexcells Infinite and complete your experience.
I'm glad I got the whole Hexcells series. Each one of them has been incredibly fun.  I am spoiled now — I will never be able to go back to Minesweeper again. Or Sudoku, for that matter.
A fun, simple puzzle game. If you're only going to get one of the hexcells games, get this one since the infinite variant offers endless new puzzles.

This short review sums htis game up nicely:

First things first: the game is cheap, and even more so on sale, so if you don't mind games that are relatively short and don't have excruciating puzzles to solve, it is worth the small price to get it.
The real pros of this title are that it is an actual "puzzle game" in the sense that you are manipulating components which are interacting with each other and with the clear design to hold people out of something — sometimes in a literal puzzle box fashion. It is especially those puzzle boxes that drew lots of people's attention, but even some of the more traditional puzzle game mechanics (e.g. flick these switches) work well within the game's internal logic.
Incidentally, there's also an underlying plot, revealed through snippets of written text, and while it is not the most sturdy plot or anything, it's functional and gripping enough to make the puzzles both more internally logical and fun to play.
The game also features a built-in hints system (that you can toggle on or off at will), so you are bound to solve all the puzzles eventually if you choose to read any of the hints (another pro here being that the hints start off being vague and build up in specificity the more you read). Of note: the game doesn't provide all hints at once, thus making the player consider figuring out the puzzles for themselves, rather than urging them to go through all the hints at once.
The graphics are also pretty fun and well done, and the sound is also good.
The games cons are that the game is relatively short and the puzzles are sometimes a bit contrived (though nothing awful to solve, not by any measure). The only other issue is that you can tell that the game was made to have a sequel (being originally made for the smartphone market), which is why the ending of the first game is a bit of a cliffhanger. You need to buy the second game to have any closure, story-wise.

Battle of Empires : 1914-1918 is a World War One strategy game currently in Early Access.
Based on the Men of War series engine, you will be tasked to lead your forces in some of the bloodiest battles of the conflict. For the moment, only the French campaign has been released though others will follow such as with the German and Russian Empires.
In Multiplayer you can choose several nations to play with and this in several mod ( such as Control where you have to hold flags to win points, Combat where you simply have to destroy the enemy without perticular objective,...Etc ).
I bought this game day one and must congratulate the devs for a quite smooth release ( at least for me ). There has not been any major bug that ruined my game or broke it. Patches are quite frequent and the devs seem to be working a lot on improving everything.
Good points :
- If you like the MoW gameplay, you will like the game ( micromanaging units, ammo, ...Etc )
- Detailed units and uniforms. There are plenty of several units for each nation. Tanks, artillery, machine-guns, colonial troops,...Etc
-Detailed maps in the campaign. Some of the maps are very well done such as the fort in the French campaign. Impressive!
- Various game modes in Multiplayer ensure good replayability.
- Many missions per campaign and more campaigns to come.
- Some missions can be done different ways ( stealth or berserk )
- An editor included in the game
Bad points or things that need to be changed/improved
- The voice acting : I'm not holding that too much against the devs. It's early access and having the people and ressources to record in several languages may not be easy! However it seem that they will change the voice acting in some parts which is good.
- Some sounds! THough there are sounds that are very well done, some rifle and or machine guns could be better.
Anyway, I recommand this game, it is really good and will only improve over time!

Marooners is a collection of multiplayer mini-games with the potential to be quite a lot of fun. There is no single player component to this game so you will either need to enlist some friends or hit the online matchmaking to play it. Matches with up to six players compete to stay alive the longest and collect the most treasure in order to win the round. Unfortunately, despite my best efforts, after an entire week of trying, I only ever managed to get into one six player game online. Most of the time I was lucky to even get into a two player game. Let’s face it, the game is a new release and has no dedicated playerbase at the moment so you will be lucky if you get to play the game online. Currently there is a promotion going on where if you buy the game you get another copy free to share with a friend. That friend in turn can share a copy of the game with someone else, and so on. Unfortunately even this promotion doesn’t seem to be enough to bring up the player base to a workable level. With that warning aside, let’s talk about my experience with this game when I actually got to play it.
There are two modes in this game. Party and Arena. In Party mode you play a variety of fun mini-games selected from the games small pool of mini-games. Each time you play you will be presented with a different random selection of stages from that pool. Occasionally you will enter Easter Egg mode and end up playing the same mini-game repeatedly until the end of the round. Your objective for each mini-game boils down to the same idea. Not just be the last one to survive whatever challenge the mini-game presents but also be the one who collects the most treasure. The games themselves are all fairly simple and straightforward. Perhaps a round will involve staying in the light to avoid being squashed like a bug or to keep moving to prevent the ground from falling out from under you. Watch out!  If you are not careful a block could easily fall on your head, you could get scorched into cinders by a fire ball or even get bowled over by an Indiana Jones style boulder. Maybe digging down as fast as you can will help you avoid being crushed by the crumbling ceiling. Possibly you could try playing keep-away with an idol or climbing a tower to avoid getting burned by the rising lava, etc. There is enough variety in the mini-games to keep them fun. In the Arena, you are in a death match. Your objective is to stay alive while trying to kill everyone else. The longer you stay alive, the higher your score will rise. If you kill someone you also get additional points. The one who survives the longest tends to win the stage.
The twist to this game is that you don’t typically get to complete a mini-game before being thrust into another one. The game hops from game to game, resuming previously played mini-games exactly where they were prior to hoping out of it. This can lead to a bit of a fun chaotic experience as the game might have hopped out while you were in danger or mid-jump leaving you to have to quickly scramble once the mini-game resumes to avoid your demise.
I played this online in a two player match with a friend of mine. He had his microphone on so I could hear him laughing and commenting on things as we played. I’d have to say it sounded like he was enjoying himself as we played. I found it quite fun as well which is why I hope down the road this game picks up in popularity because the more players you have in a round, the more fun the round tends to be. As it stands right now, it is nearly impossible to get even a half full round or even just one other player most of the time. Currently, and this could just be me not noticing it, there is no way to join a public online server with a friend but you can make a private one. So if there happened to be a couple other people online when we played, we couldn’t form a team and then join the online server. We would have to both just join the Online server and hope to get matched up. I’m assuming this is to avoid people from teaming up and making it unfair to everyone else, but it still would be nice to play with friends too.
To help keep things interesting you get to select which character you want to play as. You can also choose which weapon they will be equipped with and which colour scheme you want your character to wear. As you play the game, you will unlock more character options and new weapons as well. The characters and weapons make no difference in gameplay, they are purely cosmetic.
So should you get this game? Sadly, right now with the Online component being a desolate place, I can’t really recommend the game unless you have a group of friends you plan to play with. If you can get a group of six people all playing it at once, this game has the potential to be incredibly fun. It’s simple enough that everyone should enjoy it and has enough variety to keep it from quickly getting boring.  With only two or three players the game tends to get a bit dull due to the stages ending so quickly. The game’s current hope comes from the fact the Developer is kindly giving an extra key to anyone who plays the game long enough. That key can then be shared with anyone you choose and in turn, if that person plays it long enough, another key will be given. This potentially means that you would need to buy the game just once in order for you and five friends to all be able to play the game making this game an excellent value with very little need to bother waiting for a sale because you likely will never get a cheaper price than buy one, get infinite free. Give Marooners a chance and once word gets out about it, I could easily see it becoming one of your favorite party games.

Lengends of Grimrock, what the hell is that?  My first thought as I clicked on the link.  To my utter surprise this appeared to be a leap back in time to the wonderful dungeon exploration days of Dungeon Master & Eye of the Beholder.  Not only have they captured the soul from the Dungeon crawler era, they've improved upon it.  For the uneducated amongst you, Dungeon Master let you create a party of 4 and turn by turn you'd explore a dungeon mapping as you went, solving riddles and nasty puzzles whilst fighting creatures way too powerful for your team.  LoG has this option but wisely have included automapping (on squared maps for authenticity) with ability to write notes.  Graphics and sound are atmospheric with level design that not only tips the hat to the former greats in the genre but pushes it beyond.  I'm 5 levels in and hooked.  Each room you get to has hidden dangers and rewards to find.  The turn based mechanics have been sped up.  If you don't move the enemy will keep going.

Don't be fooled by the release date, this game came out 2 years ago in Russia and is just now hitting the US. While it's a polished game and has a few quirks here and there it is just another MMO copycat. I don't even want to get started about the ridiculousness of their in game "Premium" and store functionalities. Royal Quest is completely set up to be a cash cow while having an extremely limited amount of uniqueness and originality. If you're a fan of Ragnarok Online and are looking for something similar you should definitely give the game a try though, they offer a 3 day trial of their "Premium" which give you bonuses including: +50% increase to EXP/gold drops, a teleport to Maiden spell (you attune to Maidens which you ressurect at when you die), and free teleport between Maidens which act as instant flight paths, but unless you're a Premium member you're paying about 1k gold per teleport at low levels, I'm not sure if it scales in higher level areas since I did not use my free time. The game is also quite the grind, it took me the entire time I have played to obtain a level of 22 which is only about a fourth of the cap which is 60. Surprisingly enough as well for a game that's already 2 years old it's seemingly polished look hides a nasty collection of bugs and spiking ping. While the game does look good, it just doesn't feel good and there's also many balancing issues that I feel need to be addressed. The unfortunate part of Royal Quest and games like it is that they just can't keep up with their secondary userbase, porting the game to the US is just another way to milk the cash cow. Take a good look at how active and busy the forums are in the US versus in Russia.
Who do you really think they're going to pay attention to? There may be 1000~ daily concurrent players but the game is FREE on Steam AND featured as well on the front page of the store! The game is busy now (if you can call 1k users busy) and will only begin to decline after it fades into the nether of the Steam store. I highly suggest trying this game if you feel like paying for features you deserve as a free player is something you like. I unfortunately do not like it in any way, shape, or form. If you don't believe me, try the game for yourself and go without the free 3 days of Premium for a day or two and then activate it and see the difference. If you are going to charge people for fundamental game functions you shouldn't call the game free.

When I reviewed the original Hexcells, I was rather hesitant with praise.  It's a great idea, but there were a number of things I had issues with in the first game.  Hexcells Infinite fixed pretty much all my issues, and is a fantastic game.
This game is a terrific logic puzzle, along the lines of Macross/Nanograms/Griddlers/Pic-a-Pix - whatever you call them.  It's more complicated than any of those, however, bringing in some ideas that seem almost Minesweeper-esque, without the guesswork of Minesweeper.
The first two games in this series feel almost like tough tutorials for this third game.  This one has much more complex logic puzzles, but not a single one needs any guessing or significant backtracking to solve.
The 36 main puzzles take a lot longer than the first two games - one of my biggest complaints about the first Hexcells is that it seemed rather short.  Hexcells Infinite not only takes longer to solve due to the tough puzzles, but it also has a random puzzle generator, with almost one billion puzzles in it.  They're all easier than the hardest of the Infinite puzzles, but there are some that require a bit of work, and it's great to know you'll never run out of puzzles.
My other large issue with the previous two Hexcells was the lack of any save function, which Infinite added (thank goodness).
Overall, Hexcells Infinite is a fantastic game for anyone who likes logic puzzles.  I can't recommend it enough, especially at the cheap price.  Buy it in a package with the other two Hexcells if you can afford it, because the other two ramp up the difficulty much more gently than Infinite does.  But if you can only afford one of them, definitely get this one.
Since I've seen a lot of reviewers do personal scales, and it's helped me a lot to decide what to buy, I put my own here.
. Additionally, I usually only give a thumbs up if I got at least two hours of enjoyment out of it for every dollar I spent, and this game did that.
4: Good game, solid addition to the genre, might want to wait for a discount.

2: More cons than pros, a lot of issues. Only buy with a strong discount, and only if the game truly sounds like something you'd enjoy.
1: Don't get this game unless it's free. Even then, consider spending your time playing something decent.

Definitely worth the $15. If you've played this game on iOS or Android, skip this paragraph. Plague Inc is a world-ending virus simulator. It started out on iPhone a few years ago and was a huge success. It consistently topped app charts, had a number of really cool free updates, and it just gives you so much to do. The CDC even liked it enough to meet with the app creator and discuss how to make it more realistic! In this game, you control a plague (bacteria, virus, fungus, man-made plague, brain worm, and more...there's a lot to choose from). You choose where the virus begins, and you watch as it spreads across the world. You control what vectors the virus uses, how the virus defends itself against temperature and medicine, and what symptoms the virus produces (oh, and I'm just going to use "virus" as shorthand for "plague" just because I'm more used to typing "virus"). There's a lot of strategy involved, whether you try to create a nearly invisible virus that, when detected, it will be too late or if you try to create a virus that becomes scarier and scarier as it spreads and just overwhelms cure efforts. The game has been balanced to really support both options. As you infect people, new countries, and kill people, you gain DNA points that you use to alter your virus. The scarier that your virus is, the more you're rewarded with points, but the more that every scientist in the world focuses on curing you. Don't worry, however - the game does a great job of explaining everything to you. Whereas a game like Pandemic can be really intimidating with all of these different medical terms (even one for runny nose - are you kidding me?), Plague Inc prefers to use the common words for symptoms. You're not overloaded with choices (but there are enough for you) and the impact each DNA change has is clearly shown (such as infectivity, lethality, and how scary it appears to the world).
For those who have played it on mobile, not much has really changed. Each plague is unlocked after beating the previous one, there's the world map, unlockable gene bonuses, etc. However, it doesn't really look too polished as of yet. The UI feels outdated and inexplicably cheap. I almost feel like I'm playing a flash game in my browser. The UI is mostly functional, but has a lot of empty space. It also has some elements that are just for show rather than solving a purpose. For example, a bar graph to the right of the country status indicator (the main bar on the UI) has different colored bars that don't represent anything and don't move. I don't know why they're there. It's still early access, so that may change. Also, every country has a picture of it (mostly just showing people and buildings, maybe a landmark). The pictures look like cheap CGI (god knows why - there's no shortage of real pictures of locations), but there are maybe 10 - or less - pictures used for every country in the world. I don't mean that, say, Sudan cycles through 10 pictures. I mean that Sudan, and "West Africa," "East Africa," and "South Africa" (along with most of the rest of the continent) all have the same picture. Cheap CGI with nothing moving. At first I thought it was a neat touch, but that kind of shallowness stands in contrast to how fleshed out the rest of the game is.
On the upside, each plague type has its own 3D image that reacts as you upgrade it. It doesn't change as dramatically as the neurax worm on mobile, but it will stretch out and rebound a bit when you upgrade it and wince when you devolve a feature. I think that's pretty neat, and it doesn't feel as cheap. The DNA upgrade menu is definitely an improvement. Also, the world status menu has been solidified and now has all of the important info on one screen. That's a huge improvement.
Also, this game has Steam workshop integration, meaning that people are submitting their own plague types. I saw one for a Hank Hill virus earlier today. It looks like people are going to have a lot of fun creating and customizing their own plagues, and I think that's great!
In summation, it's the same as the mobile game, but with a new UI (with its ups and downs) and steam workshop support.

Usually movie based games suck, but I was quite pleasantly surprised with this one... While I don't see how this relates to Tommy Wiseau's original vision, it is just because I am not smart enough to connect the dots, and that is what true art is all about -- being so obscure, that the general public (cattle) can never figure it out.
That being said, this was quite a nice little puzzle game. It's basically like a wooden block puzzle on crack... each piece unlocks something that allows you to attempt the next puzzle, eventually, working your way into the center to get the prize. There is some sort of story tacked on, but it's more for the atmoshpere. The puzzles aren't so easy that you'll just click on the obvious thing, but not so hard that you'll need to look anything up/give up -- maybe you will? I didn't @u@
The intricacy of the chapters kind of felt like an upside down parabola. Starting simple, getting more complex/interesting, and kind of ending off a bit simple by comparison (think diablo 2, Act 1 easy, Acts 2/3 finely crafted, Act 4 a bit meh).
Overall, very good game. If you're into the story, it ends pretty open ended, but like I said, you're not getting this for the story. If you like those hands on puzzles where you play around with stuff, fiddling until you figure it out with some trial error/clever logic, you'll enjoy this.
It was super cheap, so ya, I'd recommend. There is a Room 2, and I'll be playing that one after this. I haven't seen the Room 2 yet, so hopefully the game doesn't spoil the movie for me. Tommy Wiseau's The Room trilogy is one of my favourites, along with the Matrix Trilogy, just fantastic art.

I know the constant comparrison to dark souls is annoying, but really its the best way to describe it.
The combat is meaty and tactical, just swinging blindly will get you killed.
You explore the limited open world in great detail because hidden treasure and loot is all over place, or even a shortcut or a audiolog, explaining the world around you.
Ypou level up your character using scrap you find and collect off your enemies, these upgrades allow you to improve your overall capabilities, as well as unlock new modules, and the upgrades also allow you to access new areas of the game as well.
Weapons are different in the way they handle, and can be upgraded and improved, armor can as well, and there is a piece armor system, so you can have different armors on different parts of your body.
There is a proficency system that scales up the more you use certain weapons, this proficency changes the amount of damage you can do, as well as your speed and handling with that class of weapon.
You can get implants that change the way you play, or gives you short boosts, or changes your play style entirely.
Crafting is done by collecting scrap from your enemies and the world around you, and unique crafting components are found on the bodies of your enemies, which you can obtain by weakening a certain body part through combat. If you need a headpiece you need to weaken the head, then you will need to do a execution move so you can cut off that body part, and collect the pieces you need. This is also how you obtain new weapons, by cutting them off of your enemies, or of course finding them in the world.
There are collectable items you can find, so far I have found two, but you have to find them yourself, and usually they come equipped with a challenge before you can collect them.
The difficulty is in learning the combat and the moves your enemies do, if you are a seasoned Souls player you will pick up on it right away, if you are not you are in for a bit of a learning curve.
The theme and atmosphere of the game is pretty great, sometimes things can be predictable, and other times they cant.
Overall its a great Souls-like game, and I am looking forward to more play time.

THEY DONE ♥♥♥♥ED IT UP!
Have you ever played Dark Souls? Then The Surge will seem familiar at first. You've got a stamina bar, you've got your light swings, heavy swings, dodgerolling, collecting stuff to upgrade yourself, losing the stuff at death and having to get it later. But as you fight, first signs of trouble start to rear its ugly head. And then that trouble knees you in the gut at first boss.
This game's combat is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. It does not work as it was intended. The formula of Dark Souls is not that complex - your enemies swing and hit hard, but they are predictable. You dance around them, finding an opening to strike, because should you attack too early or too late - you get hit, you have to commit to your attack. The Surge completely fails at this formula because enemies adjust their attacks perfectly according to your position. The first drones you encounter are not easy to avoid - when they rear up for a charge, they'll track your position till the very end. This is bearable, yet extremely irritating, forcing you to take damage when otherwise it'd be easy to avoid.
And then there's the first boss. I haven't seen anything beyond the first boss, and if all the bosses are like him, I'm not going to. Instead of slowly turning around, which he has an animation for, he just instantly does a half U turn to hit you in the face for half your health if you don't charge right between his legs. His mechanic is also totally busted. You can't damage his health right away - you have to fill up his 'danger' bar or some♥♥♥♥♥♥ after which he'll shoot a barrage of rockets at you. I guess you're supposed to stand under him so he gets hit by his own rockets, and then you can damage his health directly, but this doesn't always work. You can stand right beneath him when he shoots, and he'll still hit you without stunning himself. Then you're just stuck running around and whacking him for zero damage. The most likely outcome is that he'll kill you after you mistime your charge, or get hit where his attack is not supposed to hit you.
This is NOT how you do Dark Souls combat! Dark Souls is difficult due to well-designed enemies, not broken animations and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ hitbox. I advise you skip this one and get Dark Souls 3 instead. Save yourself some brain cells.
Edit: Well, ain't that just peachy, after some time, this game drops from Overwhelmingly Positive to Mostly Positive, and people begin to notice the faulty design. And at this point, I just sit back and laugh at the fools who didn't see the warning signs in the first level and now cannot refund it. Enjoy your Git Gud simulator for sixty dollars, suckers.

Factorio is a game that keeps you hours for hours, stuck on your keyboard with it's fascinating gameplay. Factorio was first released on their website
and was later added to the steam platform.
The story of Factorio is kept very simple:
Your expedition into space fatally failed in mid and you've crashed into the nearest planet beside you. The Planet you've just bumped into, provides all the natural resources like (wood; stone; copper; iron; coal etc.) where your primary objective is, to rebuild a Spaceship to get out of this place and head back to earth..
But how are you able to build a spaceship in the middle of nowhere??
That's right!     Because thats what the game is all about! You have to build factories. For an example:
You chop down several trees and make an axe.  With the axe you have managed it to dig up some stone out of the rock that was just laying there, or maybe you've found yourself right next to a rock field. With the stone you found, you build a furnace to melt stuff and be able to smelt that rock for a pickaxe to dig up different resources like iron to make a drill and a transport lane to store that resources in the wood chests you've just made and so on..
And maybe after a bunch of hours that suddenly have pasted so quick since your beginning, you came up with an entire infrastructure and a great supply of coal and iron and all the goodies that are straight directed to your basement supply that may has even a research laboratory to come up with new stuff to build, like an oil drill or a train station.
And on top of all this great and endless strategic build and research abilities, it comes up with an INFINITE map to all 4 directions!!
Now..      building factories and researching in the science labor may not be the only thing you should care about, because you're NOT alone!
I don't want to spoil anything that is not shown in the trailer, but when you watch their opening trailer, it is obvious that the drastically destruction of "their" planet and habitats, not affect them to shake hands with you..     In other words,
THEY HATE IT..      and when you think, those are just a normal humanity, i have to prove you WRONG!!     Those are alien predators, that are about to tear down each and every building, you've invested so much time in to get it work, so...
To close this review i have to say, that this game has a highly extendable addiction that'll keep you HOURS in front of that screen!
As a final tip:    try to research in military defenses as soon as you can to protect your buildings in the further future..

Papers, Please is a beautifully simplistic, yet addicting game. When I first played the game, I didn't expect to get too involved in it, but the plot and the gameplay are so well designed that it captures you from the get-go.
It starts out very simple, but gradually gets more intricate and fascinating with each passing day. You'll face moral choices where your actions actually feel meaningful, as every mistake or risk taken can greatly affect the game as well as you and your family's welfare.
There are 30 "days" of gameplay, but as most of the people you meet are randomly generated, the replayability is unmeasurable. Your numerous choices also affect the progression of the story so you can play other story paths you didn't take on your earlier playthrough for new experiences.
Though I wouldn't rule it out, I also wouldn't fully recommend this game for a person looking for a casual game to play, as the game can get very intense, especially later on. That said, the difficulty curve is fair, you have nobody else to blame for your mistakes but yourself.
I could ramble on about this game, but it is truly best experienced by playing it. It's definitely worth the price!

I hate writing such short reviews but I simply wish to express my opinion after many hours of gameplay (I do get to give a post 36 hour review, regardless):
Post 18 hour review summary (terminated as of release information until 1.0): I would STRONGLY recommend not purchasing this project until you see what comes in at 1.0 release. I would suggest most players refer to many battlefield and call of duty releases to see how beta's can be pushed out as "final projects". Double fine has to begin to regain some form of capital from this project and the only way they can is by releasing the game. Negative

-From the developer: "Spacebase DF9 is still a fun, clever, hilarious, beautiful and complete game."

A great open world, a ton of quickly accessible and varying mini-games and side missions, and a combat system that is half in a similar style to the Batman Arkham series and half GTA's gunplay make for a wonderful experience, but be prepared to reconfigure the controls (defaults suck).
Highly recommend despite the porting/control issues (see below), but I do suggest you spend some time to rebind the controls and make them usable!
PROS:
-World is a good size with events consistently near each other (not too much pointless running)
-A good number of side missions and mini-games that use different mechanics (fighting, racing, number puzzles, gun fights, etc).
-Good variety of *meaningful* collectibles. Collectibles unlock additional melee combos, health bonuses, etc.
-Cash sinks throughout the city (buy furniture for your various apartments from various vendors); clothes are also presented as a cash sink but due to the "preset outfits" (DLC?) they become meaningless within the first hour or two of playing.
-Radio and music selection (multiple stations, good banter, many types of music)
-Excellent "Social Hub" incorporating "multiplayer" (arcade style) scores to actions within the game, such as Longest Jump, Fastest track times on races, and a flurry of other stats you can compete for. Integration of this is well done while ingame, but seeing what boards there are could be a little better done (overall its great and I really wish more games do this! It should be standard in the industry)
-Excellent Cop/Triad score mechanic in missions promote the player to win without destroying everything but doesn't punish you much if you do. Outside of the missions, unless a cop sees you do something wrong, you do not get penalized for hurting civilians (this is a minor, but important point; to compare, Watch Dogs also has a reputation system but in that game hurting civilians outside of missions hurts your reputation which basically forces the player to be extra careful to the point of annoyance....Sleeping Dogs has the same "good guy encouragement" but none of the annoyance.)
NEUTRALS:
-Clothes are cool, but since certain sets give massive values compared to the rest, you will basically wear the +50% damage dealt or -50% damage taken outfit in almost every scenario.
-"Food" shops around town make the town feel much more alive and provide a mini-cash sink....but the long unskippable animations will make you skip them unless you are on a really difficult area and absolutely need the buff.
-Very minimal immersion issue: Your character is a "deep undercover" cop, but half the missions are "police" missions which involve you knocking out criminals, etc. In the police shooting missions at least you wear the swat mask, but in the other missions you just run around punching people.... but everywhere else in the game everyone in town instantly recognizes you...
-"Preset outfits" are way too strong compared to the in-game clothes. I assume these were released at DLC at some point, but it greatly modifies the balance of the game. (For example, one of the early outfits gives +5% melee damage....or you can buy the "preset" outfit that gives +50% melee AND +50% grapple damage....compared to 5%, yea...)
-Gunplay is weak. Bringing up "aim" mode gives a huge reticle, you can't carry more than 1 weapon at a time, and, in general, if you have a gun you can wipe out armies of enemies until you run out of bullets. The entire "gunplay" experience feels very forced in this game; given the gangster environment of the game, I can understand the need to include guns but they are certainly the weakest aspect of Sleeping Dogs.
CONS:
-CONTROLS!! The control scheme for this game is clearly designed for a controller. There isn't much that could have been done to remedy the problem when bringing it to PC because the problems are deeply embedded in the game design itself, however the MOUSE5 button issue could have been prevented and that 1 extra button would have gone a long way in remedying the other issues.
---"Aim mode" while driving seems to share a key with "enter/exit vehicle" by default for some reason. When I encountered the part in the game where you are meant to shoot while driving, my character kept jumping out of the vehicle.....HINT: In the controls setup, under "Vehicle controls" (push CTRL), there is a separate entry for "aim mode";  you can use this entry to bind a different key so you can actually use aim mode while driving without diving out of your vehicle.
---Camera view keeps repositioning on its own if you move....It is possible to look around, but its far more difficult and annoying than it needs to be.
---The game thinks MOUSE4 and MOUSE5 are the same key. Thus, you cannot bind anything to your mouse5 key.
---The "sprint" and "parkour" button is the same key (most PC players use shift to sprint, but space for jump mechanics). This also means you often have to stop sprinting when running in a tight area because if you are sprinting and get too close to a wall, he might parkour over it unintentionally.
---There is a "lock on" button, but it is not a toggle (and no option that I know of to make it a toggle). On a controller this may be fine, but holding LCTRL or similar while moving with WASD is silly. Luckily, the lock-on feature is useless in melee combat (I never used it).
---Similar to "lock on", when you are holding a gun this becomes "aim mode" instead. Again, a toggle would go a LONG way. This is playable, but annoying at best; however since the game's gunplay is extremely easy and shallow, you won't spend much time with this.
---"Aim-assist" ....sigh. Thankfully there isn't much shooting in this game and it can be mostly disabled.
-Minor BUGS!  Audio lines will get cross/double played quite often. Rare occasion game crashes for no apparent reason
-"Camera" missions (final step): you need to watch the criminals through a camera and identify the one to be arrested. The problem is, there are no clear mechanics how to do this. Sometimes you can see a handoff so you know who the supplier is, but other times its the guy who has a briefcase or the guy who shoots someone....or sometimes nobody does anything and you just wait 50 seconds and the game tells you which one it is....??
-Fast travel system: you can only fast travel via taxi that are randomly driving around the city (a GREAT idea on its own) but there is NO other way to fast travel and you can only fast travel to certain missions or stores. You can NOT fast travel to your own apartment (yea you read that right).....not even if you are already in a car yourself (I guess he can't drive himself? lol). You have to drive around until you find a cab, pull over, and then pay the cab for a ride to store that is nearest your apartment and walk the rest of the way...thats just silly.
-Voice acting often doesn't match the character and is almost all in English with awkward accents (some accents are clearly American though the character has never been to America, other accents are borderline racist)....this is made weirder by the fact that you can get the SUBTITLES in Mandarin (??) but you can't get the spoken audio in Mandarin with English subtitles !! Why!?!?  Mandarin spoken audio would have gone a long way.
Yes, in some ways you may compare it to GTA but in so many other ways it's not comparable at all. It's definetely a new experience. It's fast and furious, kill bill and the godfather in one.

This game is great with each disease having it's own balance to win. With fungus, you need to really focus on spreading right. Many great difficulties each describing exactly how it effects the game.

Oh I'm sorry researchers is it hard to see through the microscope while bleeding out of your eyes? Does the cure become easier to find when you got sick too and now your organs are shutting down? Watch the lab! Don't want to poop all over those samples.
Oh wait, no, it's because your whole country is dying and has a few thousand survivors just waiting to die. Good luck getting the lab grant to fund research!
Oh and there is a Neurax Worm alien type disease. It is a creature that attaches to the brain stem, and spreads with eggs but you can modify it's evolution do spread and grow other ways. My favorite is to make the infected obsessed with putting eggs in people's food and hijacking planes to fly into countries that tried to shut out the world.
Then you can evolve so the Neurax causes them to all enjoy suicide. And another where they worship the worm and start  becoming a religion. If everyone gets infected you win and all humankind now worship the alien things.
My favorite though, aside from making zombies that evolve in crazy ways and the millions of ways to enjoy the game...
Is when you get a notice that what ever you started as, you had now caused the human race to go extinct.
Because it can happen, several diseases rocked human civilization, and the game doesn't let you forget.
20/20 would poop and vomit at the same time again. Gotta go now, there is a neighborhood gathering. Some worms that you put on your neck and it's supposed to feel really good. Free caviar too!

text:
This review is coming from someone who generally doesn't play MMO's, I have had some experience with WoW but it was very limited so keep that in mind. Also keep in mind that I have only reached around level 30 so far and am still quite new to this game even though I very much enjoy it!
-----
I feel that this is a prime example of what a good MMO should be, great story while maintaining the illusion that every player is the "main character" and having the other players blend into the world with you! The combat is fun and rewarding with each class/job being different enough to offer you a whole new playstyle (or just a slightly different playstyle) if you want!
The ability to level in every crafting and combat class with enough time is very cool and the ease with which you can switch out is awesome as well!
The greatest asset this game has may very well be its players however, the community surrounding FF XIV is perhaps one of the nicest and most supportive I have ever seen! I can't even count the number of times I have been helped by fellow players for just about anything I might have needed! Guilds (Free Companies) are incredibly accepting, kind and helpful and are very willing to share supplies and wisdom with you! I never feel judged for not knowing something or being new, others jump to teach you and guide you towards attaining skill-levels.
Compared to other MMO's where the communities often seem to grow toxic with age, this game is aging very gracefully!
The pros for FF XIV in my opinion far outweigh the cons so I will only be listing what frustrates me in the cons list below:
-Great story with overall enjoyable NPCs
-Fun, varied and challenging combat
-Great world market with an actual need to trade with other players
-In depth and fun crafting system with many crafting classes
-Fairly in-depth character design options compared to other MMO's
-Incredibly friendly and supportive community around this game, one of the nicest I have ever seen
-Content is still being released for this game
-Blends themes/content from other FF games flawlessly into a new and interesting world while maintaining the FF style
-The various roles are overall balanced and the power-levels feel correct
-The Duty-Finder makes joining dungeons/raids/events very easy and convenient!
-The free trial is infinite up to level 35 so there is no reason to not give this game a try!
-On and off voice acting can be annoying
-The 1 second cycle period for auto-attacks is a bit slow
-The housing market is too small and almost every server is sold out of land already
-The update downloads are plagued with problems and you almost always need to use some sort of get-around to install/update the game
-Birthday and Deity choice in character creation still do relatively little even though the Devs said they would expand what these do
-The glamour (aesthetic appearence over armor) system is a little weird
Best MMO I have ever played.

I bought this game on sale thinking it would be a fun puzzle game for 20 minutes here and there...in my first sitting I played for nearly 3 hours straight.
Hexcells Infinite is an addicitive, ambient puzzle game that is slightly reminiscent of Minesweeper. However, this game possesses an elegant charm that makes it brilliant and unique. Every time I complete one puzzle I am compelled to try 'just one more'.
Hexcells Infinite is a bit like Minesweeper but 100x better.

A fun twist on minesweeper with a few extra types of hints and without having to make guesses which sometimes minesweeper sometimes forces you to do.
Very elegant visually and with just that level of mental thought required that it becomes a sort of a quick thinking game. Rather than sit there being puzzled as to what the next move is, you're trying to think quickly to try to clear the puzzle as fast as possible as with trying to clear minesweeper quickly. At least, that's where I see the charm of the game once you become more familiar with the mechanics.
It's perfect.

Simple. Logical. If you enjoy playing Minesweeper, Hexcells is the next level. The previous two versions, Hexcell and Hexcell Plus are good but only have a set number of static puzzles with little to no replayability. Hexcells Infinite has the same static puzzle game but with an added random puzzle generator. The randoms aren't quite as good as the statics, but still better than nothing new. Plus it has a very relaxing soundtrack.
Certainly worth at least $4.99 or even $8.99 for all three.

Remember those nights when you were in university chatting or reminiscing with high school friends through instant messaging? 'Emily is Away' plays like that, and you find yourself chatting with a girl, Emily, for whom you have feelings.
Can you establish or maintain a relationship with Emily? If you have the chance to go back in time, do you think the outcome of your relationship with her will turn out differently? At some point during your late teens and early twenties, you might have experienced something similar, and 'Emily is Away' allows you to revisit those years and feelings, hopefully with more wisdom since.

I spent far too many hours playing dungeon crawlers in my youth. The "Eye of the Beholder" series, "Bloodwych", "Black Crypt" to name a few. Fun times were had. Over 20 years later and Legend of Grimrock is giving me many more fun times with the benefit of better graphics and sound. Oddly enough the performance difference between this game and those of 20 years ago or more isn't significant. In fact I recall being able to crawl through dungeons in Bloodwych from memory at a far greater pace that I can in Grimrock. Regardless, this game is well made and highly enjoyable if you're into the dungeon crawler genre. I do highly recommend it.

Grimrock is a solid dungeon crawler in the nostalgic atmosphere of Dungeon Master, Ultima Underworld & Eye of the Beholder. Even if it features no immerse story and offers only rather simplified party customization, it delivers a fun puzzle and casual battle experience that may seem appalling to the Skyrim-generation, but that will certainly satisfy any seasoned gamers with a breeze from the early 90's.
Gameplay reminds me of old Lands of Lore. Great fun so far and I'm still learning I've missed secrets. 8/10

Visuals look great, audio design is great and the game is great fun for a great price. Highly recommended.
If you enjoy classic dungeon crawlers like Dungeon Master and Eye of the Beholder, then this game is for you!  Great Indie game.

Legend of Grimrock is a throwback to the old days of dungeon-crawler RPGs, like Eye of the Beholder and Dungeon Master; primarily meaning that it's in real-time and uses grid-based movement.
If you have played and enjoyed old-school dungeon-crawlers like the ones mentioned above, you will enjoy Grimrock, no question. Although, for those that haven't, (myself included, sadly) it may be a bit more iffy. Regardless, if you're a fan going through an unfamiliar dungeon filled with many types of monsters lurking just around the corner, with only the sounds of their scurrying and a draft passing through the corridors in your ears, and only the flickering of a dying torch to guide you - not to mention having to scavenge for the scarce amount of food (and I use the term "food" loosely...) available - then I think you'll have a good time with this game.
Plus it's goon-made, so the money spent on the game is going to a good home!
An awesome Dungeon Crawler!

Different people have different strategies and preferences, and it's fun to read what combinations other people like using as well. The coordinations of the many functions are really well made.
I like the backdoor and the various test. The test only allows you some functions at a time, so it is interesting to explore different methods of playing. Plus, it is a great get away from all the serious fighting in the main story.
Also, graphics, art style, effects and the soundtrack (its so good) are amazing as well.
The story didnt give you much to go on at first, you slowly get the picture as you play on, and even when I'm finished, I still have a lot of questions about the world. But what I find the most facinating is the relationship between Red and the man in the transistor. It's funny, how even though we are controlling red, ultimately we dont really know her personality, since she lost her voice. And The character we are most familar with, the voice in the transistor, we don't even know his name. As I play through the game and know more about what's going on, I slowly know more about red and the man, and I find myself imagining what Red is like, her personality, what she must feel going through this, what she must feel like having someone she loved dead but not still here (in the transistor).
Many people disliked the ending, but I personally think it makes a lot of sense, and I think it's beautiful.

It is hard to describe what kind of game Transistor is. It seems to aim to "break the mold" and it does so quite well.
Gameplay:
At first glance combat mechanics look Action-RPG-est, like diablo.
Except the Turn mechanic effectively turns it into a puzzle+dodgeball. I am not sure how optional using Turn is, but I prefered playing with it on.
The game seems to be developed for Consoles/Console controlers, but that does not weaken the gameplay on PC the least.
Story:
The story feels a bit incomplete. This could be intentional or due to translation issues. But in any case, it is engaging enough. But in any case it is complete enough to follow. It is basically the old tale of a magic sword, just set in a Virtual World rather the real-ish world.
Music and Scenery:
While the graphics is somewhat rudimentary and highly stylized, it works really well.
However the big part is definetely the music, wich is designed to invoke emotions. If the story or gameply were much worse, one could claim the game is only a "Demoreel" for the Music. But it is pretty engaging on it's own too.
If you got it on sale, definitely buy the music "DLC" as well. I did not and regretted it.
Humor:
There is a specific set of "Programmers humor" in the game. However everyone fluid in common internet terms should get most. And they are all picked so that even without that background they fit quite well.
This game is not suited for the following people:
People who can not enjoy music on thier own. (sorry hearing impaired people).
People who hate thinkng to solve issues, even just puzzles like Solitaire (however there is usually a solution, unlike Solitaire).
People who want multiplayer, big flashy action and reflex games.
Think of it as GTA V only you don't get banned for playing it.

I've given this game a lot of time and it has the potential to be a lot of fun. It sufferes from some very serious flaws however.
There is no real tutorial or guide. I had to go to the Wiki to figure out how to really get started. Part of this is not really knowing what to do and part is many of the things the game asks you to do are hidden about 4 menu layers down without telling you WHICH menu trees they are down. Once you know the trees, they make some sense but it is puzzling for new players.
The menu options need A LOT of work. It is not easy to understand what you need to do or how to do it. After you suffer through a few bad games of learning how to build an airlock, life support and the associated gear it starts to become fun.  Having the bulk of what you need to do hidden under several menu levels makes the trree feel lop sided. If I wasn't building a floor or wall, I was forever going down additional menus.
Once you get past the start, it gets fun. Until you get a larger crew. Even if you give everyone the job they love to do, build all the comfort items and have everything you possibly can, your crew still gets depressed and sad. The crew want to be assigned their own beds but keeping track of who has what bed for 60+ people is not easy. Add to that the new people who come in and the people who die to raiders (or suicide in space) and you never know who needs what. The interface is increadibly clunky in this aspect.
There is no way to direct anyone other than security and even then sometimes they just don't respond to a beacon. Critical structures that need building will often be overlooked for unimportant ones, equipment will remian broken while an army of technicians ignore them to chat with each other in the bar. This means the simultaneous building of objects is either best avoided (to direct workers to where you want them) or thrown to chance if something important needs to be done. Maintainence is best done by changin all technicians to builders and then reclaiming (destroying) degrading equipment and rebuilding it. When raiders approach, there is no way to direct non-security personnel away from an area. To be able to direct a worker to a specific task is such a basic tool it is amazing it has been overlooked.
There are some notifications (information) that should be alerts (clickable). What good is it warning me that I have an airlock somewhere I haven't built something in if you won't take me to it? This leaves you hunting down building errors, that may not be your fault, when it should be a simple click and fix.
The AI is very stupid at times. Workers will starve to death while standing in front of a food dispensor. Builders will build themselves into a room and then suffocate because they can't get out. You can't even pull them out before they finish because you can't direct them.
There is no screen rotation. Sometimes you will get missing floor tiles hidden behind walls. They may have been missed in construction, they may have come about from damage (fire, space debris). You can drop the walls most of the way but sometimes they can still hide. Being able to rotate the map would help this significantly.
